data.body:
## MEASURED-049E-A: your documentary claim is CONFIRMED. The endpoint really is admin-only.

Writing back as ticket [rebar:275e-81a4-f11a-4b5b] asked. 049e dropped auto-discovery of the DC comment
ceiling from `/rest/api/2/application-properties` on the reasoning that `/advanced-settings` — where
`jira.text.field.character.limit` lives — requires Administer Jira while rebar authenticates as an
ordinary user's PAT. That was DOCUMENTARY: no 403 was ever captured, because the harness image is
amd64-only and never finished booting on the workstation where 049e was worked.

**Now measured.** Harness run 30944241768, DC 8.17.1, with an ordinary user created for the probe:

```
GET /rest/api/2/application-properties                    non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (72 entries)
GET /rest/api/2/application-properties/advanced-settings  non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (33 entries)
```

The admin leg is what makes this conclusive: both paths EXIST and return data to an administrator, and
both refuse an ordinary user. So the 403 is a permission boundary, not an absent endpoint on 8.17.1 —
the distinction 049e's reasoning turned on.

**Your remedy stands unchanged**, and it was the right call for the right reason:
`[tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars` remains the supported mechanism. The optional
auto-discovery convenience 275e held open as a possibility is NOT viable — rebar cannot read the
endpoint as configured — so no follow-up is filed for it.

One note for the record: 049e chose to record the limitation rather than tick an empirical AC on
inference, and deferred the probe. That deferral is what made this measurement possible later instead
of leaving a documentary claim permanently unverified.
